ServerSettings.Title: Server Settings
ServerSettings.EcoGnomeModExplanation1: Eco Gnome is capable of reading data from your Eco server to accurately calculate the prices of your items. It extracts skills, crafting tables, modules, items, and all recipes. It can read both modified vanilla data and data added by external mods.
ServerSettings.EcoGnomeModExplanation2: To do this, you need to download and install our server mod, [EcoGnomeMod](https://github.com/Eco-Gnome/eco-gnome-mod), on your Eco server. Once your server is restarted, a file named eco_gnome_data.json should be created in the root folder of your game server. You need to retrieve this file and upload it using the button below.

Snackbar.UploadPartiallyNokEnd: Review your mods and server edits. You can contact Eco Gnome admins for help.

ShoppingList.ReuseChoicesExample: E.g. Flour is already made at the Mill for the Bread → the Huckleberry Pie makes it at the Mill too.

ShoppingList.GuidedDesc: One choice opens the whole chain down to what can't be crafted. When there are several recipes, it stops and asks you.

ShoppingList.AutomationMaxHint: Maximize this output given the input constraints (recipes + items + input limits)
ShoppingList.AutomationRulesHint: A value = priority target, served first. MAX = maximum output with the remaining capacity (takes priority over empty fields). Empty = automatic: follows the recipes on what's left, reduced if a limit is reached.

CostMin.Tooltip: The cost related to this crafting table for each minute of craft. Represent the fuel consumption, parts replacement, eventual crafting fees...

Fuel.CalculatedCostPerMinuteTooltip: Calculated from table consumption, fuel energy and fuel price.

MarginPercent.Tooltip: The margin percent that will be applied on your sale price. Check the 'Margin Calculation Type' tooltip option for calculation details.

Rounding.Tooltip: Round margin prices to clean values for in-store display. Steps: $1-$2 → 0.25, $2-$5 → 0.5, $5-$100 → 1, $100-$1000 → 10, $1000+ → 100. Below $1 stays unchanged. Marketing rounds up then subtracts 0.01 (e.g. $4.99, $99.99) — except in the 0.25 tier where the grid is kept as-is.

NonSkilled.Tooltip: Unlock the list of non-skilled recipes in the recipe selector.

HideBlueprints.Tooltip: Hide blueprint recipes from the items to sell.

LevelAccessible.Tooltip: Only display recipes that are allowed by your skills levels.

ApplyMarginBetweenSkills.Tooltip: When the system retrieve the price of an ingredient, if this ingredient is from an other skill that the current recipe, then it's margin price will be used instead of it's production price. This allows a more fair production price for other citizens that does not have both skills.

Tooltip.2: MarkUp (default): you sum the CostPrice and Margin*CostPrice/100 to get the SalePrice
Tooltip.3: Gross Margin: The Margin percent is the percent of benefit of your SaleCost, that is capped between -99.99% and 99.99%.

CalorieCost.Tooltip: The cost of the food you eat, for 1000 calories spent in a craft. If you buy only salads that brings 700cal for 5$, then Cost per 1000 calories is 1000 * 5 / 700 = 7,14$

BuildingPlanner.Title: Building Planner
BuildingPlanner.WipTooltip: This tool is still under development: results may differ from the game.
BuildingPlanner.NoData: The building planner needs building data (occupancy, block tiers, room and housing configuration). Update [EcoGnomeMod](https://github.com/Eco-Gnome/eco-gnome-mod) on the server to the latest version (export version 5), then upload the newly generated data file.
BuildingPlanner.Hint: Shortcuts work while the mouse is over the plan · Furnishing: places furniture; blocks and rooms are built in Structure mode · Tools: 1 select, H pan · Placing: click places the chosen object, Shift+click places it again · Rotation: R / Q rotates the selected object, else the one to place · Selection: click or double-click an object or a room; drag an object to move it, arrows: one cell, Del or Backspace: delete it · Picker: middle click picks the object under the cursor (type and rotation) · Eraser: hold right click to remove objects as you go; Shift+right drag: those in an area · Drop the tool: right click on empty space; Esc drops the tool, deselects and closes the panel · View: wheel to zoom; Alt+drag or middle drag pans · Levels: PgUp/PgDn, wheel or click on the elevation · History: Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z redo, Ctrl+S save
BuildingPlanner.Rotate: Rotate (R, Q the other way): the selected object, else the one to place

FormRot.Label: Rotation
FormRot.LowSide: Low side of the form (the triangle on the plan)

Tool.room: Room (P) — drag a rectangle: floor on the current layer, walls and ceiling, in plain cubes of the material; the height option gives the air layers
Tool.box: Box (2) — drag the rectangle; centred on the current layer, height in the options
Tool.sphere: Sphere (3) — drag the radius from the centre; centred on the current layer, it extends as far above as below
Tool.cylinder: Cylinder (4) — drag the radius from the centre; centred on the current layer, height in the options
Tool.line: Line (6) — straight line on the current layer (for a slope, change the z of point 2 in the card)
Tool.curve: Curve (7) — drag from end to end, then move the mouse to bend it and click; the handle stays draggable when selected
Tool.pencil: Pencil (8) — places blocks cell by cell, with the chosen form
Tool.eraser: Eraser (9) — removes blocks one by one as you go: a pencil cell is taken out, a block of another volume is carved; Shift: places blocks
Tool.cut: Section line (0) — drag a line, then click an eye for the viewing direction

Settings.Title: Plan settings
Settings.Help: Apply to the whole plan. To save: plan menu, or Ctrl+S with the mouse over the drawing area.
Settings.ResidentsHelp: With {n} resident(s): total ×{m}, and the first {n} rooms of each category count fully.

Level.Name: Level name
Level.HeightHelp: Empty: level height from the plan settings. The next level starts right above, with its floor layer.
Level.DetectHelp: Slabs detected in the building become levels: each level spans from its slab to the next one. Untick a slab to merge it into the level below; heights stay editable. Validate only changes the levels: no room and no block is created.
Level.DetectNone: No slab detected: build the building first in Structure mode.
Level.DetectLowSlab: A slab sits on layer 1: it is ignored (a level has at least one air layer). Lower the building by one layer to use it as the ground.
Level.DetectTruncated: More than {max} slabs: only the first {max} become levels.

Rooms.DetectionSkippedHelp: Building too large for live room detection: existing rooms are kept and still checked by the analysis, but new air pockets are no longer found.
Rooms.FillEdgesHelp: Places a cube, in the material of the neighbouring block, in every air cell of the room that sees the outside diagonally (often under the steps of a roof), as players do in game. The room loses a little volume but its average tier rises, since these empty edges count as tier 0. The outside does not change; Ctrl+Z undoes it.

Housing.PropertyInfo: Already present elsewhere on the property: × {percent}.

Housing.SupportCapInfo: Support category: at most {percent} of the primary category {category} ({primary}).
Housing.TierCapInfo: Tier {tier}: soft cap at {softcap}. Above it, each extra point of value counts less and less.
Housing.SoftCapped: Room value reduced from {from} to {to} by the materials (tier {tier}, soft cap {softcap}): −{percent}.

Housing.CategoryCapInfo: {category} rooms can be at most {percent} of the value of the primary rooms (currently {rest}). Dropping value from {before} to {after}: −{reduction}.

Ai.Title: Generate a building with AI
Ai.Help: Describe the building: size, storeys, materials, style. The result is a regular plan, editable like any other.
Ai.EditHelp: Describe what to change: the AI starts from the current plan, hand-drawn or generated, and only touches what you ask. Ctrl+Z undoes the change. "New building" replaces the plan.
Ai.Example1: A house mostly in mortared sandstone with hewn log accents, modern architect style, flat roof
Ai.Example2: A medieval cottage in hewn log, one storey, gable roof
Ai.Example3: A 12 by 8 brick workshop with large windows and a mezzanine

Issue.NoRoomDefined: No room detected: a room is an air pocket fully closed by blocks (floor, walls, ceiling). Build one in Structure mode, for example with the Room tool (key P).
Issue.RoomTooBig: Room « {room} » is too big: a cell is more than 70 m from its starting point.
Issue.NoCeiling: Room « {room} » is not covered at height {height}: an air cell has no block above it. Its objects count as outdoor.
Issue.VolumeTooSmall: Room « {room} » is too small (volume must be at least 3).

Assumptions.Title: Assumptions of this version
Assumptions.Rooms: Room: any air pocket closed by blocks, as in the game. No automatic floor or ceiling: everything built comes from the placed volumes.
Assumptions.Forms: Forms (stairs, roofs, windows…): full cubes for rooms and for the cost, as in the game. The form is the one picked in the palette; its variants (corner, T…) follow the neighbouring blocks, as with the hammer.
Assumptions.EmptyEdges: Empty edges: air seen diagonally from a room counts as tier 0 and does not make it leak (setting forced by the game).
Assumptions.Holes: No open window: a missing block in the shell makes the room leak. For a window, place a glass block or a window form.
Assumptions.Terrain: Flat terrain at height 0, counted as tier 0: a block placed on layer 0 replaces it, a subtraction on layer 0 digs it.
Assumptions.View3d: 3D view: blocks and objects use the game's models when they exist, else a coloured cube. A click there selects an object or a volume, editable as on the plan.
Assumptions.Culture: Cultural multiplier of the deed: ×1. Admin boosts: 0.
Assumptions.Deed: One deed fully owned; objects outside rooms form its « Outdoor » room.
Assumptions.Efficiency: All objects enabled at 100 % operating efficiency, no dynamic value (picture frames…).
Assumptions.Talents: Lavish / Frugal talents on room tier requirements are ignored.
Assumptions.Modules: Module tier bonuses come from the modules installed on each table type in your default data context.
Assumptions.Rotations: Four 90° rotations only; free-yaw objects are approximated.
Assumptions.Tie: Room category ties are resolved by catalog order.

BuildingPlanner.Hint3d: Shortcuts work while the mouse is over the view · Camera: drag orbits around the pointed spot; right or middle drag pans; wheel: zoom toward the pointed spot · Recentre: double-click the pointed spot (the camera-facing cutaway goes through it too); Fit to screen reframes · Selection: click an object or a block (its volume); Del or Backspace, R / Q as on the plan · Move the selection: arrows follow the camera (↑ away, ↓ toward you); PgUp/PgDn up or down one block · Layers: PgUp/PgDn with nothing selected, wheel or drag on the elevation (current layer in blue); its arrows rotate the viewed side; ⤓ button: hide above the layer · Camera-facing cutaway: C · Esc: clear the selection, then back to the plan · History: Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z redo, Ctrl+S save
BuildingPlanner.HintArch: Shortcuts work while the mouse is over the plan · Tools: 1 select, 2 box, 3 sphere, 4 cylinder, 5 disc, 6 line, 7 curve, 8 pencil, 9 eraser, 0 section line, P room, H pan · Drawing: drag draws the volume, centred on the current layer (blue in the elevation); Shift+drag inverts add / subtract · Form: the palette form applies to every block of the volume (room and subtraction: plain cubes); R / Q rotates the selected volume, else the form to place · Room: any air pocket closed by blocks (floor, walls, ceiling); the Room tool builds one, floor on the current layer, the height option giving its air layers · Curve: drag from end to end, then the mouse bends it and a click places it (right click or Esc: cancel); when selected, its round handle is draggable · Eraser: hold right click or tool 9, block by block (a block of a volume is carved); Shift+right drag: an area of the layer; Shift+eraser: places blocks, like the pencil · Selection: click a volume, drag to move it, arrows: one cell, Shift+PgUp/PgDn: one layer, Del or Backspace: delete it · Copy / paste: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V on the selected volume (pasted under the cursor, on the current layer) · Picker: middle click, on the plan or in the section, picks the material, form and rotation of the pointed block · Layers: PgUp/PgDn, wheel or drag on the elevation; its arrows rotate the viewed side · Section: a click follows the tool (Select: the visible volume; Pencil: place blocks; Eraser or right click: remove the visible block; hold = stroke) · Volumes in the section: drag draws the volume in the cut plane (the height option becomes the depth, centred on the plane; a cylinder takes the cut axis) · Section line: tool 0, drag to place it; drag its line to move it; an eye flips the view direction, clicking the active eye closes the section · View: wheel to zoom; Alt+drag or middle drag pans; I shows / hides the background image · Drop the tool: right click on empty space or Esc · History: Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z redo, Ctrl+S save

EcoMarketManagement.Title: Eco server market prices
EcoMarketManagement.Help: Eco Gnome reads the average prices of the Eco server's market from its web server (the address the mod reports at each start), to suggest them next to buy prices. Set an address only if the reported one is wrong, for example behind a reverse proxy.
